identity.real_world_identity_notes: Mercedes-Benz CLK LM of 1998, the GT1 car running the naturally aspirated GT108B 4,986 cc V8 with a six-speed sequential gearbox.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and no automatic blip on downshifts. The downshift was accepted with no pedal input, so no blip is needed to engage the gear, and a clutch is still needed to pull away.
This class reports a single configuration; the selection screen offers no aero package and only the plain identity has been observed.
The car does not blip its own downshifts. An earlier drive recorded that it did, from a measurement that could read the driver's throttle as the car's blip.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mercedes-benz-clk-lm.20260815t234325634z-7a6a292a by Jason Kinslow.

The automatic blip was re-measured on 2026-08-18 in AMS2 1.6.9.91, observation ams2.mercedes-benz-clk-lm.20260818t040207012z-4b0694be. The car does not blip: the first reading was the old measurement seeing throttle carried in before the lift. The downshift was still accepted with no pedal input, so no blip is needed to engage the gear.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by a registered source.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the CLK LM and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source gives a 6-speed sequential, and the live drive selected six gears through a sequential stick with an automatic cut and no automatic blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Sequential stick, one gear at a time. The car cuts the upshift, and nothing blips the downshift, though the gear will engage unmatched. Blip anyway: it is the difference between the car settling into the corner and the driven wheels locking as you turn in.
